name: Picular
one_liner: Free color search engine that turns any keyword into hex colors pulled from top Google Image results.
what_it_offers: Type a word (e.g. 'tomato') and Picular shows the dominant color of each top Google Image result (about 10) as a hex swatch, plus an overall primary and secondary color. Results live at shareable URLs (/s/<term>). You can copy hex codes, pin up to 8 favorites into a palette, and share that palette as a link or to Pinterest. It's free, needs no account, and was built by Swedish studio Future Memories.
tech_stack: Next.js (App Router, Turbopack build) on Vercel; Google Images thumbnails (gstatic) analyzed behind an internal /api/search endpoint
portfolio_fit_reason: A quick, free way to find one or two anchor hues from the ideas behind a personal brand. It only returns single dominant swatches, with no scales, pairings or contrast checks, so it helps only at the very start.
client_ok_note: There are no terms, but hex values aren't copyrightable, so the colors can go on a commercial site. Never reuse the Google Image thumbnails shown as sources.
best_use_for_portfolio: Search two or three words that describe your work or a client's brand (e.g. 'terracotta', 'blueprint') to pick an accent color. Then build a full scale from it, check contrast against your text and background, and set it as the portfolio's accent token.
tier_reason: Returns single dominant swatches from keywords, with no scales, pairings or contrast checks. Useful only for a first anchor hue.
score_rationale: A fun, fast way to find the colors people associate with a concept, which helps with brand ideation. But it only gives single swatches, not complete accessible palettes, tokens or pairings, so it adds little beyond early exploration.
free_tier: Everything: unlimited keyword color searches, hex codes with copy, shareable result pages, pinning up to 8 favorites and sharing the pinned palette. No account.
commercial_use_license: No terms or license page (/terms, /privacy, /about and /license all return 404). Hex values aren't copyrightable, so colors can be used freely on a commercial site, but the source thumbnails are third-party Google Image results and must not be reused.
agent_friendly: None official. No llms.txt (404), docs or public API. An undocumented internal JSON endpoint (/api/search?query=<term>) returns primary/secondary hex, per-image hex colors and a last_updated timestamp, but it's unsupported and shouldn't be relied on. Agents can fetch /s/<term> pages or just use hex codes a human copies.
maintenance_signal: Live, with a recent Next.js (Turbopack) build served from Vercel cache (x-vercel-cache HIT). Tested 2026-09-14: /api/search for 'tomato' returned primary #F44409 with last_updated 2026-01-01. One sloppy detail: og:image and twitter:image metadata point to http://localhost:3000. No public changelog or repo.
caveats: Colors come from whatever Google Images returns, so results are noisy and can change over time (results appear cached; 'tomato' was last refreshed 2026-01-01). Only dominant colors, with no palette harmony, shades or contrast checks. No API, terms or license page. Social preview metadata is broken (points to localhost).
unverified_fields: tech_stack image-search backend provider (SerpApi claim not confirmed; only Google gstatic thumbnails observed)
maintenance_signal (no public changelog; rebuild date inferred)
